title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཆེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 175)
shelf_note: A Derge woodblock folio of a pramāṇa commentary (perception, inference, svalakṣaṇa, memory-ascertainment), so it belongs in the Tshad ma section of the Tengyur.

ocr_errors.image: སྤྱི་དེ་ཉིད་ནི་གྲུབ་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེའི་བདག་ཉིད་དུ (as far as I can read it)
ocr_errors.problem: connective particle ཏེ and the shad look dropped

ocr_errors.image: the cluster after ཆོས་ཅན looks like དེ་དེ་(ལྟར)… རབ་ཏུ་གྲུབ་(པའི་)ཕྱིར; detail not fully legible
ocr_errors.problem: possible misread of a small connective cluster; the sense survives

tr_errors_A.english: If that is so, it would be unestablished. Why then would inference be employed to make it known?
tr_errors_A.problem: The objector's rhetorical question ('in that case, how is it unestablished, so that inference is needed to know it?') becomes a flat statement that the subject 'would be unestablished'. That is the opposite of the objector's point, which is that the subject is already grasped by seeing.

tr_errors_A.english: Although one has apprehended only the distinct essence
tr_errors_A.problem: 'only' over-weights the particle; small shift in emphasis

tr_errors_B.english: <note>This refers to the Buddhist logical theory where perceiving an object should theoretically mean perceiving all its qualities, yet conceptual thought must still work to eliminate false impositions.</note>
tr_errors_B.problem: Interpretive commentary the page does not contain, inserted mid-argument and placed before the passage it anticipates

tr_errors_B.source: ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བའི་རྣམ་པ་དག་ལ་ངེས་པ་ (sentence runs on to the next folio)
tr_errors_B.english: why is there certainty regarding the aspects experienced as they truly are?
tr_errors_B.problem: A sentence cut off at the end of the folio is finished as a complete question. The verb, probably a negative 'does not arise', is on the next page, so the closure may invert the question.

tr_errors_B.english: the phenomena established by the conceptual mind
tr_errors_B.problem: ཉེ་བར་གཞག་པ means superimposed or imputed; 'established' blurs this

tr_errors_B.english: If so, why is it not established? By what means is inference used to know it?
tr_errors_B.problem: Awkward, but it keeps the rhetorical force ('how is it unestablished?')

pages.prefer_reason: A turns the objector's rhetorical question into a statement that the subject 'would be unestablished', which reverses the objection; B's faults (an inserted interpretive note and an over-closed final sentence) are moderate.

book_verdict: The transcription of this Derge pramāṇa folio is close to the block print, with only small particle slips. Translation A reverses the objector's rhetorical question at the turn of the debate. Translation B is sounder, but it adds an interpretive note that is not on the page.
